cohort: The study included 262 healthy pregnant women with breech fetal presentation at a minimum of 36 weeks gestation who underwent external cephalic version at Soroka University Medical Center.
finding: External cephalic version (ECV) is a safe and effective method for reducing cesarean delivery rates, with successful procedures linked to increased rates of vaginal birth, longer gestational age at delivery, and higher birth weight.
mod_finding: Successful ECV procedures were linked to increased rates of vaginal birth (p<0.001) and a reduction in cesarean deliveries compared to failed versions.
birth_weight: Higher birth weight was associated with successful ECV outcomes, though no specific inclusion range for birth weight was mentioned.
gest_age: Participants were at a minimum of 36 weeks gestation when ECV was performed, and successful ECV was associated with longer gestational age at delivery.
